chapter_note: A doctrinal chapter explaining the cosmic referents of three popular religious names ('god', 'rich one', 'angel'). Two interpretive registers are given: first, the three terms map to three types in the land of light (gods of gods summoned by the Father, the rich = call of the first gods, angels = call of the rich); second, they map to emanations sent into the contest, with angels = those sent in embassy from the three living words. Editorial frame is light — primarily 'the Illuminator said' / 'Once again hear him' attribution. Substrate dominates. The 'embassy/apostolate' language at i=32-33 is borderline but reads as cosmological mission language (cf. Third Messenger), not contemporary church mission. Editorial fatigue score reflects only the second 'Once again' frame at i=37-38, not actual register drift.
